senses.definition: Open to an idea or request, though not yet agreed to it.
senses.caution: People often hear it as a yes. If you say a senior person was amenable, make clear that nothing has been agreed yet.
senses.example: The MD was amenable to a phased rollout, though I want to be clear that nothing is signed.

cues.text: You sounded out a director in the corridor about moving the deadline and they did not push back. You are reporting that to your team without overstating what you have.
A vendor has hinted they could flex on the licence terms, and your sponsor asks how the conversation went.
You floated Christmas at your parents' rather than hers and your partner did not object. Her sister asks whether it is settled.
You asked the landlord about getting a cat and got a shrug rather than a no.

distractors: Firmly against an idea from the start.
Keen to take credit for other people's work.
Aware of something and taking it into account when you decide.
Deciding as you go, taking your lead from how things actually develop.
Unwilling to say what you think until the most senior person has spoken first.

senses.definition: Suited to being handled in a particular way, such as by automation or a simple model.
distractors: Too large to finish within the time that is available.
Already solved by a tool that the team bought last year.
Hard to measure, so progress on it cannot be shown to anyone who asks about it.
Owned by several teams at once, so nobody can make a decision about it on their own quickly.
Changing so often that any process built around it would be out of date within a single month.
senses.caution: Say which method it suits, such as automation, because the word alone leaves that open.
senses.example: The invoice data is regular enough to be amenable to a simple rules engine, so we do not need a model here.

cues.text: A dataset turns out to be clean and regular enough that a simple model handles it, and you are explaining in review why nothing more elaborate is needed.
You are telling a sponsor that the claims backlog, unlike the complaints queue, fits automation well.
A friend asks whether their messy garden could be sorted out in a weekend with the right tools, and you think it could.
